item.title: Teiger Foundation: Hosting Grant (September 2026 quarterly deadline)
item.description:
Organisation: Teiger Foundation

Location: United States. The presenting organisation must be US-based, though the originating project may have come from anywhere in the world.

Award: USD 50,000 or USD 75,000 (fixed request tiers, applicant chooses). Up to 30 percent may cover indirect and overhead costs. Organisations with annual budgets under USD 3.5 million receive special consideration for infrastructure costs. No matching requirement. No application fee.

Duration: Roughly 12 months; the 9 September 2026 deadline covers projects opening between 1 April 2027 and 31 March 2028.

Deadline: 09 Sep 2026

Funds US organisations to present curator-led contemporary visual art exhibitions and projects that originated elsewhere, on condition the presenting institution meaningfully adapts the project to its own context. Teiger's remit covers group exhibitions, single-artist surveys, participatory and community-engaged projects, digital exhibitions, and live and virtual performance, making it one of very few US funders that will directly finance media-art and performance programming at organisational level. Requests are fixed at USD 50,000 or USD 75,000 with up to 30 percent for indirect costs, and there is no minimum organisation budget size, with smaller organisations explicitly favoured for infrastructure support. Hosting deadlines are quarterly: 9 September 2026 and 9 December 2026, both 17:00 ET, each mapped to a defined project-opening window roughly a year out. IMPORTANT: re-presenting a touring project unchanged is explicitly not competitive; the curatorial adaptation is the substance of the application. US 501(c)(3) status is required and the fund is not open to individuals or non-US organisations. Teiger's larger biennial Call for Proposals is not running in 2026 and next opens in autumn 2026 with an early-2027 deadline.

item.title: Andy Warhol Foundation: Exhibition Support (Fall 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts

Location: Applicant's own venue. US-based 501(c)(3) required; international organisations must first submit a letter of inquiry before any proposal is accepted.

Award: USD 60,000 to 100,000. Direct costs only (artist payments, catalogue and publication, artist-designed public programmes); staff salaries excluded. Request must not exceed 25 percent of total direct project costs, which functions as a de facto 75 percent co-financing requirement. No application fee.

Duration: Exhibition must open between 6 months and 2 years after notification.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Supports solo, two-person and thematic group exhibitions of contemporary visual art. The Foundation explicitly prioritises artists whose work is under-recognised and whose practices are experimental or hard to categorise, which makes it a genuine route for media arts, digital culture and art-and-science exhibitions rather than a blue-chip-only fund. Grants of USD 60,000 to 100,000 cover direct exhibition costs including artist fees, new commissions, catalogue production and artist-designed public programming, but not staff salaries. Applicants may request no more than 25 percent of total direct costs. The proposal is a roughly three-page curatorial letter plus detailed direct-cost budget, organisational budget and IRS documentation. Deadlines are 1 March and 1 September annually, with notifications 1 July and 1 January. IMPORTANT: this is a postmark or email-timestamp deadline, not a portal deadline. Fiscal sponsors are explicitly not accepted; the applicant must hold its own IRS ruling letter. The six-month-to-two-year timing rule is strict, so a September 2026 application suits exhibitions programmed from mid-2027 onward.

item.title: Andy Warhol Foundation: Multi-year Program Support (Fall 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts

Location: Programming delivered by the applicant organisation. US 501(c)(3) required; international organisations must submit a letter of inquiry first.

Award: USD 60,000 to 100,000 across two years. Request must not exceed 25 percent of the organisation's annual operating budget. No formal match, but the 25 percent cap means the balance must come from elsewhere. No application fee.

Duration: Two years of programming, beginning after the 1 January 2027 notification.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

This is the closest thing in US foundation philanthropy to core support for an organisation running an ongoing public programme, as opposed to a single exhibition. It funds a two-year slate of exhibitions, residencies, public art, screenings, performances, lectures and publications, which means a recurring festival or convening series can be underwritten here. Grants are USD 60,000 to 100,000 over two years and may not exceed 25 percent of annual operating budget. The Foundation states a preference for organisations supporting artists with experimental, hard-to-categorise practices, putting digital culture, sound art and art-and-science programmers squarely in scope. Applications require a forward programme schedule covering at least the twelve months after the award, a three-page narrative focused specifically on how artists benefit (the stated central evaluation criterion), a full one-year organisational budget and 501(c)(3) documentation. Deadlines are 1 March and 1 September, notifications 1 July and 1 January. Fiscal sponsors are not accepted. Organisations that received a Multi-year grant within the past year are ineligible, and proposals centred on anniversaries, relocations or major renovations are explicitly discouraged.

item.title: Andy Warhol Foundation: Project Grants for Small-Scale Organizations (Fall 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts

Location: Applicant's own venue or programme, with a mandatory public component. US-based only.

Award: USD 20,000 to 30,000 toward direct costs such as artist payments and production. No application fee.

Duration: Project must complete within one year of notification; September-round projects may begin 1 January 2027 or later.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Launched in February 2026 as an expansion of the Foundation's programme to reach organisations too small for the Exhibition Support and Multi-year strands, and it is the single most relevant new US scheme for small media-arts festivals. It funds visual arts projects with a public component, explicitly naming film festivals, exhibitions, installations, residencies and interdisciplinary collaborations. Grants are USD 20,000 to 30,000 toward direct costs. The hard gate is the USD 200,000 annual operating budget ceiling plus US 501(c)(3) status held directly by the applicant, not via a fiscal sponsor. The Foundation states it assesses creative risk-taking and the growth of participating artists rather than community impact metrics, which suits experimental sound and digital culture programming. Proposals are a maximum of three pages plus a one-year operating budget, a project budget and IRS documentation. Deadlines are 1 March (projects begin 1 July or later) and 1 September (projects begin 1 January or later). Youth-focused projects are ineligible. One project per round, and grantees must wait a year after project completion and final reporting before reapplying.

item.title: City of Moorhead: 2026 Call for Public Art (Movable Interactive Piece)
item.description:
Organisation: City of Moorhead, Minnesota

Location: Moorhead, Minnesota, USA. The piece will be sited at different locations throughout the city. No geographic eligibility restriction is stated in the call, so non-US artists appear eligible, but this is not confirmed in writing.

Award: Not published. The call announcement states no budget, commission amount or artist fee, and the linked Request for Art document could not be retrieved. Confirm the budget with art@moorheadmn.gov before investing time in a proposal. No application fee is mentioned.

Duration: Single commission; timeline not published

Deadline: 04 Sep 2026

The City of Moorhead is seeking proposals for an inspirational, movable public artwork to be installed at rotating locations across the city. Interactive elements are explicitly encouraged, with kinetic sculpture, digital installation and tactile elements named as examples. Strong proposals invite public participation, promote creativity and youth engagement, are safe for all members of the public, are durable enough for year-round outdoor conditions, and draw people to gather. Submissions are reviewed and ranked by the Artist Review Team, whose recommendation passes to the Art and Culture Commission and then to City Council for the final decision. Questions go to art@moorheadmn.gov. Proposals are due by 10:00am on Friday 4 September 2026.

item.title: Cafe Royal Cultural Foundation: Performance Grant (Summer 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Cafe Royal Cultural Foundation NYC

Location: New York City (five boroughs), or a location in close proximity to NYC approved by the foundation, USA

Award: Up to $10,000 for production costs (performers, collaborators, rehearsal and venue rental, design elements, technical staff, etc.). Does not fund the creation or composition of new work. No application fee.

Duration: Production grant; performance must start no sooner than 1 November 2026 and complete by 22 September 2027

Deadline: Closed 03 Aug 2026

The Cafe Royal Cultural Foundation NYC Performance Grant supports individual artists producing theatre, dance and performance art (which may be accompanied by music) moving toward a public performance. The Summer 2026 cycle offers up to $10,000 for eligible production costs: actors, dancers and guest performers, director/choreographer/composer and creative-team fees, costumes, lighting, sound, scenic, props and set, rehearsal and venue rental, and production and technical staff. Funds do not cover the creation or composition of new work; if the performance is a play it must be a full production (readings do not qualify). ELIGIBILITY: individual performers only (not groups or organizations) who are US citizens or resident aliens, current NYC residents who have lived in the city at least one year and will remain through project completion. This cycle accepts only 40 applications and closes early if that cap is reached. Applicants may submit up to 5 video links. Apply via the foundation's performance page. Deadline: 3 August 2026, 9:00 am ET (or earlier if 40 applications are received).

Open call details

item.title: Alabama Historical Commission: Clotilda Memorial Public Art Commission
item.description:
Organisation: Alabama Historical Commission (with Forecast Public Art)

Location: Africatown, Mobile, Alabama, USA; open to artists internationally.

Award: USD 2,000,000 total project budget for a paid public art commission. No application fee.

Duration: Permanent public art commission

Deadline: Closed 09 Aug 2026

The Alabama Historical Commission, working with public-art consultancy Forecast Public Art, seeks proposals for a major memorial artwork honoring the survivors of the Clotilda, the last known ship to illegally traffic enslaved Africans to the United States (1860). The memorial will convey the survivors' lives and legacies and be developed through collaborative community engagement with historic Africatown, the community founded by Clotilda survivors, and the broader diaspora. ELIGIBILITY: open to artists of all disciplines, including time-based and media artists; individuals and teams; open internationally. BUDGET: USD 2,000,000 total project budget. DEADLINE: 9 August 2026, 11:59pm CST. Applications are handled through the CODAworx RFQ platform; find the Clotilda Memorial listing in the CODAworx opportunities index. Verify the listing details on CODAworx before applying.

item.title: The Factory on Willow Funded Artist in Residence
item.description:
Organisation: The Factory on Willow

Location: Manchester, New Hampshire, USA

Award: Furnished studio apartment with heat, hot water, electricity and internet, plus a USD 350 travel stipend and a USD 1600 stipend toward food and art supplies

Duration: 12 weeks (about 3 months)

Deadline: Rolling / undated

The Factory on Willow is a non-profit funded artist residency in Manchester, New Hampshire, housed in a 90,000 square foot mill building from 1904. The 12 week program supports amateur and emerging artists of any medium to develop their current projects and creative practice. Selected artists receive a furnished studio apartment with utilities and internet, a USD 350 travel stipend, and a USD 1600 stipend covering food and art supplies. The residency runs in three annual sessions (March to May, June to August, and September to November), with two artists selected per session. Each residency concludes with a public capstone showcase, and participants donate one work to the Factory's permanent collection. There is no application fee and applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

Open call details

item.title: CERF+ Emergency Relief Grants
item.description:
Organisation: CERF+ (The Artists Safety Net / Craft Emergency Relief Fund)

Location: United States and US Territories

Award: USD 3,000 one-time grant

Duration: One-time grant

Deadline: Rolling / undated

CERF+ provides Emergency Relief Grants of USD 3,000 to craft artists in the United States who have experienced a recent and substantially disruptive career-threatening emergency or disaster. Eligible applicants are individual craft artists aged 18 or older who have lived and worked in the US or US Territories for the past two years and who make original three-dimensional visual art objects by hand, including folk and traditional art forms. The grant is a one-time non-taxable gift with no reporting required on how funds are used. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, though the program will not fund applicants if too much time has passed since the qualifying event. There is no application fee. Artists may receive one grant per emergency, no more than one per calendar year, and up to four grants over their lifetime.

Open call details

item.title: Rauschenberg Medical Emergency Grants
item.description:
Organisation: New York Foundation for the Arts (NYFA) / Robert Rauschenberg Foundation

Location: United States (remote application)

Award: One-time grants up to USD 5,000

Duration: One-time grant

Deadline: 17 Nov 2026

The Rauschenberg Medical Emergency Grants, administered by the New York Foundation for the Arts on behalf of the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation, provide one-time grants of up to USD 5,000 to help artists in financial need cover recent unexpected medical, dental, and mental health emergencies. The program is open to generative visual and media artists and choreographers working in visual arts, film, video, electronic and digital arts, and choreography who live anywhere in the United States, the District of Columbia, a Tribal Nation, or a U.S. Territory. Applicants must be artists in financial need, with adjusted gross income at or below USD 80,000 for an individual or USD 160,000 for joint filers, and must not have received a Rauschenberg Medical or Dancer Emergency Grant in the past five years. Eligible expenses include emergency medical bills, diagnostics, consultations, therapy, prescription medications, emergency dental care, and transportation to appointments. The grant does not cover lost wages, general living expenses, or care for anyone other than the artist. Applications are accepted during defined cycles, with the current cycle running roughly from late October to mid November.

item.title: Illuminations Grant for Black Trans Women Visual Artists
item.description:
Organisation: Queer|Art

Location: United States; open to self-identified Black trans women and trans femmes working in visual art and based in the US.

Award: USD 10,000 to one winning artist, plus USD 1,250 each to four distinguished finalists. Winners and finalists also receive additional professional development resources and guidance, and each judge conducts a studio visit with the winning artist.

Duration: One-time award

Deadline: Closed 02 Jul 2026

Now in its 7th year, the Illuminations Grant for Black Trans Women Visual Artists is an annual USD 10,000 grant from Queer|Art that provides critical support to Black trans women whose work has often been under-recognized in the visual art field. To further recognize finalists for their artistic achievements, Queer|Art also provides a USD 1,250 award to four distinguished finalists. Winning artists and finalists receive additional professional development resources and further guidance to bolster their creative development. The grant was developed and named in partnership with Mariette Pathy Allen, Aaryn Lang, and Serena Jara, and is made possible entirely through support from visual artist Mariette Pathy Allen, whose photographic work over the last forty years has focused on expanding cultural consciousness around gender and transformation. It is administered through Queer|Art with a rotating panel of judges, each of whom conducts a studio visit with the winning artist as part of the award's focus on creative and professional development; judges for the 2026 cycle include Jordyn Jay, Isis Awad, and Utē Petit. ELIGIBILITY: qualified artists must be self-identified Black trans women and trans femmes working in visual art and based in the United States. Deadline: July 2, 2026.

Open call details

item.title: MSB Interpretive Panels: Public Art Commission (Creative Philadelphia)
item.description:
Organisation: Creative Philadelphia (Office of Arts, Culture and the Creative Economy)

Location: Municipal Services Building, Center City, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States. Philadelphia-based artists strongly encouraged; artists from outside the region considered. Multiple in-person site visits required (travel costs covered within the project budget).

Award: Total project budget of USD 250,000, which must cover: artist fees (18% design fee), design and engineering, fabrication and installation, structural footings/anchoring, travel and site visits, AR development (software, hosting, content production), insurance (1%), community engagement participation, and a service warranty keeping content compatible with new mobile OS versions for a minimum of 10 years. No application fees.

Duration: Permanent public artwork commission; two-part selection process.

Deadline: Closed 12 Jul 2026

Creative Philadelphia announces a call to commission a series of permanent interpretive panels with integrated augmented reality (AR) components at the Municipal Services Building in Center City Philadelphia. The commission is part of a broader initiative that includes an upcoming public sculpture of Dr. Sadie T.M. Alexander by artist Vinnie Bagwell. Inspired by Alexander's groundbreaking legacy in public service, these interpretive panels will celebrate the City of Philadelphia's municipal employees (past, present, and future) and provide deeper context for understanding Dr. Alexander's impact; they will be located in front of the building's landscaped areas, flanking the upcoming sculpture, and are intended to complement and support the overall site experience. SCOPE: an artist team will design and fabricate four (4) permanent, sculptural interpretive panels incorporating augmented reality (AR) elements to expand storytelling beyond the physical surface of the artwork. ELIGIBILITY: all interested artists are invited to apply; Philadelphia-based artists are strongly encouraged, though artists from outside the region will be considered; multiple in-person site visits are required and associated travel costs must be covered within the project budget. SELECTION: a two-part process: Part 1 submission of qualifications; Part 2 finalist proposals and interviews. Up to three (3) finalists are invited to submit short concept proposals and attend an interview; at no point should artists submit design proposals. BUDGET: USD 250,000 total (see amount for the required cost breakdown). An Artist Informational Meeting is held via Zoom on 30 June, 6:00-7:00pm. Application questions: paige.phillips@phila.gov. Apply via Submittable. Deadline 12 July 2026 (submissions close Monday 13 July 2026, 6:00 AM).

item.title: WSW Artist's Book Residency Grant
item.description:
Organisation: Women's Studio Workshop (WSW)

Location: Rosendale, NY, USA; in-person residency.

Award: $350/week stipend; up to $1,000 for materials; up to $250 for travel within the Continental US; free onsite housing; 24/7 studio access. No application fee.

Duration: 8-10 weeks; residency runs September through June, one year after application.

Deadline: 15 Nov 2026

Women's Studio Workshop (WSW) offers an eight- to ten-week residency for artists to produce a limited-edition artist's book. Working intensively in WSW's studios in Rosendale, NY, selected artists print and bind their own books; edition size must be between 50 and 100 copies. AMOUNT: $350/week stipend; up to $1,000 for materials; up to $250 for travel within the Continental US; free onsite housing; 24/7 studio access. WSW provides technical advice, training on new equipment, techniques, and materials, and production assistance. SALES CONTRACT: 20% of the edition goes to the artist; 20% (at least nine copies) stays with WSW for archival and institutional sales; 60% goes to general distribution and sale. If the artist sells through WSW, WSW takes a 30% commission plus 20% for marketing; the artist receives a 50% commission, paid annually around 30 June. WSW holds the right to sell distribution copies at a 20% discount to standing-order and repository institutions. WSW's books are held in over 450 collections worldwide, including the Library of Congress, Yale University, and Vassar College. An outside jury of artists and curators selects recipients. INDIGENOUS ARTISTS: applicants may check the appropriate box on the Submittable form to be considered for the BIMA Artist's Book Residency Grant for Indigenous Artists. APPLICATION MATERIALS (upload via Submittable): current resume; brief project description including media required (200-word maximum); materials budget form (Google Sheets, Excel, or PDF); up to ten images of recent work; image script (title, medium, dimensions, date). MAILED MATERIALS (to WSW at the address below): a physical book mock-up demonstrating how the book will be bound or function, actual size, with at least 1-2 fully realised spreads; and the shipping form (download and open the PDF locally). Mail to: Artist's Book Application, Women's Studio Workshop, PO Box 489, Rosendale, NY 12472. Applications open 1 August 2026; deadline 15 November 2026, 11:59pm EST; notification March 2027; residency runs September through June, one year after application. Apply via Submittable at https://wsworkshop.org/residencies/artists-book-residency-grant/.

Open call details

item.title: MAK Center: Artists and Architects in Residence 2027/2028 (MAK Schindler Scholarship, Los Angeles)
item.description:
Organisation: MAK Center for Art and Architecture, Los Angeles

Location: Los Angeles, California, United States (Mackey Apartments). Residents must be present in L.A. for the full six-month term.

Award: Six-month MAK Schindler Scholarship residency with accommodation provided at the Mackey Apartments. The open call does not state a stipend, travel or honorarium figure; confirm any additional financial support directly with the MAK Center. No application fee stated.

Duration: Six months. Residency terms run October to March or April to September; 2027/2028 cycle.

Deadline: Closed 12 Aug 2026

The MAK Center for Art and Architecture awards Artists and Architects in Residence scholarships (the MAK Schindler Scholarship) to independent projects exploring the relation between art and architecture. Projects are chosen for their ability to critically examine current trends in art, architecture and society; to make a compelling connection with Los Angeles as the place of implementing or continuing the applicant's own work; and to demonstrate a conceptual and experimental approach. Emphasis is placed on the L.A. location, and residents' projects often reflect, incorporate and address specific facets of the city and its social fabric. Recipients are encouraged to take part in the MAK Center's activities and to attend meetings, workshops and project discussions with other artists and students. ELIGIBILITY: freelance artists; fine arts or architecture students at a university who have completed the '2. Studienabschnitt'; or architects or artists who have recently graduated. Teams of up to three are eligible if all members practice together as an artist group or collective of architects, are all present in L.A. for the six months, and name a contact responsible for the team. HOUSING: the Mackey Apartments are made available to scholarship holders only; family members, relatives and friends may be accommodated for a maximum of two weeks during the term, permitted in advance by Beth Stryker, Director of the MAK Center. Eligibility is excluded if the applicant has been or will be granted another scholarship in the USA immediately before or after the MAK scholarship, or if the data form is incomplete or the required portfolio is missing. Residency terms run October to March and April to September. Deadline 12 August 2026. Apply: https://www.makcenter.org/apply-mackey

item.title: CALI Futures 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Center for Cultural Innovation (CCI)

Location: California, USA. Applicants must reside full-time in California

Award: USD 5,000 project-restricted grants, awarded competitively. USD 100,000 total available each year across the 2026-2028 funding cycle. No application fee.

Duration: Grant support period December 2026 to December 2027

Deadline: 28 Aug 2026

CALI Futures supports artists and cultural workers across California, individually and in teams, who are meaningfully contributing to alternative efforts outside of conventional nonprofit and for-profit arts and culture systems. The Fund encourages work focused on income, ownership, and care, and uplifts the role of artists and cultural workers in shaping and sustaining alternative efforts that provide greater financial stability, strengthen creative ownership, and deepen mutual support across the broader arts ecosystem. Project-restricted grants of USD 5,000 are awarded through a competitive process. Competitive applicants present (a) a clear project request; (b) proof of an active, current artistic or cultural practice; (c) a description of their contribution to an alternative effort that improves financial sustainability, creative ownership, or mutual support and addresses challenges not sufficiently solved by conventional nonprofit or for-profit sectors; and (d) framing that ambitiously describes the larger implications of this work for transforming artists' lives and future cultural possibilities. The Fund supports individuals and teams at every stage, from initial ideas to research, implementation, experimentation, and reflection. ELIGIBILITY: applicants must be individual artists or cultural workers (cultural producers, culture bearers, creatives, cultural practitioners); must reside full-time in California; must be contributing to an alternative effort improving financial sustainability, creative ownership, or mutualistic social support within the arts and culture sector; and that contribution must have occurred or begun on or after 1 January 2020. Teams are eligible, but all team members must meet the criteria and only one application is accepted per team (one member applies and is responsible for grant requirements). INELIGIBLE: individuals without an active practice; organizations seeking operating or program support; arts administrators; individuals living or working outside California; past CALI Catalyst grantees describing the same project funded in 2021-2025; incomplete applications; and those with a conflict of interest with CCI or Hewlett Foundation board, staff, or directors. The Fund is administered by the Center for Cultural Innovation (CCI) with funding from the William and Flora Hewlett Foundation. TIMELINE: applications open 9 June 2026 at 9:00 a.m. PT; deadline 28 August 2026 at 11:59 a.m. PT; review September to November 2026; notifications by 17 November 2026. Submitted via Submittable. Questions: grants@cciarts.org (include CALI FUTURES in the subject line) or 415.288.0530.

Open call details

item.title: Westonka Public Artwork Commissions (Hennepin County Library, Mound, MN)
item.description:
Organisation: Hennepin County Library, facilitated by Forecast Public Art

Location: Westonka Library, 2079 Commerce Boulevard, Mound, Minnesota, United States

Award: Two commissions (artists/teams may apply to one only). Opportunity 1 (Commerce Porch): $60,000 not-to-exceed artist fee. Opportunity 2 (Concrete Shear Wall + Trash Enclosure mural): $75,000 not-to-exceed artist fee. Each fee covers all expenses (artist time, equipment, materials, community engagement, fabrication, installation and any other project costs). No application fee.

Duration: Project across 2026-2027; new Westonka Library opens Spring 2027

Deadline: Closed 14 Jun 2026

Hennepin County Library (working with Forecast Public Art) is commissioning permanent artworks at the rebuilt Westonka Library in Mound, Minnesota. Two opportunities, with artists or teams applying to only one: Opportunity 1 - Commerce Porch ($60,000) for a sheltered outdoor gathering space (sculpture base up to 3' x 6', extending out up to 3', up to 10' high); Opportunity 2 - Concrete Shear Wall (5'6" x ~15') above the service desk plus a curved Trash Enclosure mural (~25' x 8'), with a combined fee of $75,000. The library is being rebuilt as a net-zero-energy facility, slated to open Spring 2027. Suggested themes include honouring Indigenous histories and relationships to land, revealing invisible systems (pollination, water cycles, soil life, migration), light-and-shadow play, knowledge/story/nature/memory/community, and narratives of sustainability and renewal. ELIGIBILITY: mid-career and established individual artists and teams who live within the geographical boundaries of Minnesota, including those from Native Nations whose homelands are in what is now Minnesota. Open to 2D and 3D media (sculpture, mosaic, murals). Info session and virtual site visit 4 June 2026, 5:00-6:30 pm CST (registered participants receive the recording). Contact: taylan@forecastpublicart.org. Deadline 14 June 2026, 11:59 pm CT.

item.title: WeHo Artist Grant 2027 (City of West Hollywood)
item.description:
Organisation: City of West Hollywood, Arts Division

Location: West Hollywood, California, United States

Award: $6,000 per artist (total category pool of $30,000/year, so approximately 5 awards). Funds may be used in any capacity to fulfil the proposed project within the calendar year. No application fee.

Duration: Calendar-year project; mandatory public presentation at WeHo City Hall in November 2027 plus a 3-5 minute film summarising the project

Deadline: Closed 01 Jul 2026

Direct-to-individual artist grant from the City of West Hollywood aimed at nurturing the long-term development of an artist's practice: realising work, advancing conditions of creation, and navigating the complexities of making art and making a career. The City's goal is to keep artists in West Hollywood, attract new artists, and contribute to the city's economic and social well-being. Awardees produce a 3-5 minute film describing the project and its contribution to quality of life in WeHo, and present publicly at City Hall in November 2027. ELIGIBILITY (strict): legal address must be in the City of West Hollywood (no exceptions; proof of residency may be required); applicants must be registered on the West Hollywood Artists Registry; previous WeHo Artist Grant recipients are NOT eligible; students cannot apply in their discipline of study; cannot also be funded by another City Division or Department or co-sponsored by a Council office for the same project; only one grant category per artist per calendar year; City elected/appointed officials, employees and immediate family ineligible. PROJECTS NOT FUNDED: fundraisers, capital campaigns, murals, or religious-based programmes/events. REVIEW CRITERIA (40 points): vision and clarity of project (10), impact of funding on the applicant and WeHo community (10), portfolio (10), professional resume (10); peer-review panel forwards recommendations to the Arts and Cultural Affairs Commission. TIMELINE: deadline 3pm Wed 1 July 2026; panel reviews August 2026; ACAC approves September 2026; notifications and mandatory orientation November 2026; earliest award of funds March 2027 (subject to contracting compliance). Submit two work samples (news clips do not count) plus a clear creative process and budget.
